producer_report.summary: An invocation's recorded tokens are now the sum of the result event's modelUsage over all models, and the gate checks the same sum. Before, the tokens came from the top-level usage, which can cover less than modelUsage, while the gate compared the requested model's entry. That is the 2fsa mismatch. Top-level usage is now only the fallback when modelUsage is absent. I did not see the failing record; the cause is inferred from the code and the numbers in the request. I did not touch claude.rs, invocation.rs, fake.rs or landing_tests.rs, because the fix in parse_result flows through them unchanged.

checks_run.note: The first run failed in xtask policy because I had renamed a test named in docs/enforcement.md. I restored the name, and `cargo test --locked -p xtask` then passed. All other targets passed in the earlier `--no-fail-fast` run. I did not rerun the full suite after the rename.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a new test feeds a result event whose top-level usage differs from modelUsage (a main thread plus subagent usage on the requested model). It shows the resulting invocation record passes check_invocation with no Reconciliation violation.
criteria_check.evidence: stream.rs test invocation_tokens_are_the_sum_of_model_usage_not_the_top_level_usage parses a 2fsa-shaped result event and asserts usage equals the modelUsage figures. reconcile.rs test job_2fsa_figures_disagree_but_the_all_model_sum_reconciles asserts check_invocation returns no violations for those figures. The two tests are not joined end to end: the stream test stops at the parsed usage.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a reconcile test shows that an invocation whose measured tokens genuinely disagree with its per-model usage is still flagged.
criteria_check.evidence: requested_model_tokens_must_match and the 2fsa test's first assertion (6/3136/275219/3821 recorded against 90/52656/3634696/134508) both expect one violation. usage_split_over_several_models_is_summed also flags a mismatch.

criteria_check.criterion: The invocation's measured tokens and the gate's check use one definition. The definition is stated in a doc comment: either the sum of modelUsage over all models or the requested model's modelUsage. The gate compares like with like.
criteria_check.evidence: A comment in stream.rs parse_result and the module doc in reconcile.rs both state the sum over all models. check_invocation sums models_used over all models.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check: both are clean. Existing stream and claude tests still pass.
criteria_check.evidence: clippy with -D warnings and fmt --check both produced no output. The athena-agent unit tests passed (37 passed, 1 ignored).

criteria_check.criterion: The defect's numbers (90/52656/3634696/134508 against 6/3136/275219/3821) appear in a regression test fixture or comment, so the owner can see the job 2fsa failure is covered.
criteria_check.evidence: The numbers appear in comments and fixtures in both stream.rs and reconcile.rs, and in CHANGELOG.md.

open_issues: Existing records that already carry top-level tokens that disagree with their modelUsage still fail the gate. I left them alone because re-landing job 2fsa and editing its records are out of scope.
mistakes: I renamed requested_model_tokens_must_match, which docs/enforcement.md names. The policy test failed and I reverted the name.
learnings: xtask policy test every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists requires tests named in docs/enforcement.md to keep their names, so do not rename them.
The invocation's tokens flow from ResultEvent.usage through claude.rs, so fixing parse_result covers the real driver. The fake driver is unchanged, so its path is not covered by this fix.
